Bayesian calibration

Source: R/bayes.R
calibrate_bayes.Rd

Instead of one best parameter set, a sample from the posterior: every set consistent with the record and the priors, in proportion to how well it fits. The spread of the sample is the parameters' uncertainty given the data, and runs of its sets give a predictive band.

Usage

calibrate_bayes(
  config,
  forcing,
  observed,
  lower,
  upper,
  priors = list(),
  generations = 1000L,
  chains = 3L,
  lambda = 0.5,
  log_offset = 0.01,
  ar1 = TRUE,
  temper = 1,
  warmup = 0L,
  log_scale = character(0),
  start = c("flow", "soil"),
  baseflow_fraction = 0.7,
  soil_fraction = 0.5,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

config, forcing, observed, lower, upper

As in calibrate_pdm().

priors

A named list of priors (prior_uniform(), prior_normal(), prior_lognormal()); parameters not named get a uniform prior over their bounds.

generations

Generations of the sampler; the model runs are chains x generations plus the initial archive of 10 x parameters.

chains

Number of chains.

lambda, log_offset

The Box-Cox power and offset.

ar1

Model the errors' lag-1 autocorrelation.

temper

Power on the likelihood, in (0, 1].

warmup, log_scale, start, baseflow_fraction, soil_fraction

As in calibrate_pdm().

seed

Random seed; the caller's random state is restored.

Value

A pdm_bayes list: samples (the post-burn-in sets, with log_likelihood and log_posterior), summary (each parameter's mean, standard deviation, 5%, 50% and 95% points and rhat), best (the configuration of the highest posterior), error_model (the best set's error autocorrelation rho and innovation variance s2), acceptance, and the settings, for posterior_band().

Details

The likelihood treats the errors on Box-Cox transformed flows (boxcox_flow()) as a lag-1 autoregression with normal innovations, the autocorrelation and the innovation variance set to their best values at each set. Hourly errors run on from one step to the next; treating them as independent would make the posterior far too narrow. temper, below 1, flattens the likelihood further where even that is too sure, as a power on it (0.25 counts the record as worth a quarter of its length).

The sampler is DREAM(ZS) (ter Braak and Vrugt, 2008; Vrugt, 2016): chains Markov chains that propose jumps from differences between past states, kept in an archive, with randomised subspace sampling. It suits the correlated, curved posteriors of hydrological models and needs no tuning. The first half of each chain is burn-in. rhat is the Gelman-Rubin statistic on the second halves: below about 1.2 for every parameter, the chains agree.

Each run starts as calibrate_pdm() starts it.

See also

posterior_band(), prior_uniform(), boxcox_flow()

Examples

rain <- synthetic_rain("2021-01-01", years = 1, dt = 1, seed = 2)
cfg <- modifyList(pdm_presets("standard"), list(area_km2 = 20))
flow <- run_pdm(pdm_from_config(cfg), rain[c("rain", "pet")])$output$q_m3s
flow <- flow * exp(rnorm(length(flow), 0, 0.05))
fit <- calibrate_bayes(modifyList(cfg, list(fc = 0.8)), rain[c("time", "rain", "pet")], flow,
                       lower = c(fc = 0.5), upper = c(fc = 1.5),
                       priors = list(fc = prior_normal(1, 0.2)), generations = 100,
                       warmup = 24 * 30, start = "soil")
fit$summary
#>   parameter     mean          sd       q05      q50      q95     rhat
#> 1        fc 1.002829 0.002604072 0.9952765 1.003812 1.006559 1.046141
